Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

psychnets 0.8.8

  • The articles were revised: fuller introductions, the model before the data, and references to current methodological work. Their code is unchanged.
  • The Ising and mixed graphical model articles now quote the results of the current version (they predated 0.8.6).
  • SRL_GPT cites its source correctly: Vogelsmeier, Oliveira, Misiejuk, López-Pernas and Saqr (2025).

psychnets 0.8.7

  • net_centralities() documents that the closeness of an isolated node is 0 (igraph gives NaN). No number changed.

psychnets 0.8.6

  • tmfg_certificate() tests planarity for any graph (left-right planarity test). Before, a non-planar graph that was not chordal could be counted planar. The verdict for a TMFG is unchanged.
  • ising_fit() and mgm_fit() with the native solver select each node’s penalty on glmnet’s default path, as IsingFit::IsingFit() and mgm::mgm() do. lambda_min_ratio now defaults to glmnet’s rule. Edge weights can change (up to 0.0165 on six bfi items) and now agree with IsingFit and mgm. Pass lambda_min_ratio = 0.01 for the old grid.

psychnets 0.8.5

  • as.data.frame() of grouped and multilevel results passes ... to each network, so include_zero = TRUE returns every node pair. It was ignored.

psychnets 0.8.3

  • A slow but finite nodewise logistic fit is no longer reported as separated in ising_sampler().

psychnets 0.8.2

CRAN release: 2026-11-18

New features

  • panel_gvar() estimates the panel graphical VAR model (Epskamp, 2020) from few-wave panel data: temporal, contemporaneous and between-person networks. Edges are selected with select = c("none", "prune", "ebic"). New dataset srl_panel and a vignette.
  • psychnet(within = ) estimates within-person networks.
  • net_compare() accepts two networks of one grouped psychnet() result, gains na_method, and reports the unadjusted p-value (p_raw).
  • net_stability() and net_casedrop_reliability() gain cor_method.
  • New as.data.frame() methods and what = options for stability, bootstrap, moderated MGM and panel GVAR results; summary() and plot() for multilevel networks.

Changes to results

  • net_compare() stores the network-structure test as $structure (M) and the global-strength test as $strength (S), as in van Borkulo et al. (2022). $M and $S raise an error.
  • net_stability() computes the CS-coefficient as bootnet::corStability(); net_casedrop_reliability() defaults to cor_method = "pearson".
  • ebic_glasso() refits the lambdas near the EBIC minimum before choosing one, and returns absent edges as exact zeros.
  • mgm_fit() solves gaussian nodes to optimality (weights move by up to 1e-7).
  • mgm_fit(), ising_fit() and ising_sampler() rescale weights to a maximum of 1, as mgm::mgm() does.
  • net_bridge(normalize = TRUE) divides the 2-step bridge expected influence by the number of nodes, as networktools::bridge().
  • net_split_reliability() gives a split with an empty half a correlation of 0.
  • condition() reads value in the moderator’s own coding.
  • ising_sampler() warns under (quasi-)complete separation and does not certify such a fit.

Other

  • Errors and warnings are classed conditions (psychnet_bad_input, …).
  • Ordered factors are kept as ordinal items; ising_fit() codes logical and two-level factor columns 0/1.
  • Plots use the Okabe-Ito palette and show significance by fill and line type as well as colour.

psychnets 0.5.2

CRAN release: 2026-08-23

  • Faster examples: the resampling examples use method = "pcor". No estimator changed.

psychnets 0.5.1

Renamed

  • casedrop_reliability() is now net_casedrop_reliability() and network_reliability() is now net_split_reliability(). The old names, also exported by Nestimate with a different first argument, are removed. Arguments, results and numbers are unchanged.

New

  • ebic_glasso() gains lambda_path = (a fixed penalty grid, for resampling), penalize_diagonal = (with a matching glasso_kkt() argument) and refit = ("unregularized" refits the selected graph without a penalty).
  • mgm_fit(native = FALSE) models categorical nodes with more than two levels, as mgm::mgm() does. A numeric column with 10 or fewer integer values is treated as categorical, with a warning (psychnet_type_promotion).
  • Any two-level coding ({1, 2}, {"no", "yes"}) gives the same fit as {0, 1}.

Fixes

  • The base nodewise solver returns exact zeros for inactive coefficients, so the selected edges no longer depend on the platform. One weak edge of the mixed-data mgm network goes.
  • Resampling verbs pass each draw to the estimator as a direct call would (factor columns and incomplete rows kept), and keep the observed node set.
  • cor_auto() rejects pairs with fewer than two joint observations; correlation p-values use pair-specific sample sizes.
  • Bootstrap difference tests split ties, so identical distributions give p = 1.
  • Corrected node-betweenness normalisation; relative-importance aggregation keeps direction; rank dichotomisation no longer splits ties by row order.
  • Unavailable certificates report certified = NA.
  • The glmnet paths honour nlambda and lambda_min_ratio.
  • net_predict() refuses an mgm network with a categorical node of more than two levels.
  • Node order follows the input columns and is never sorted.
  • Estimator numerics are stable within a minor version: a change to a selected edge set, or to a weight beyond 1e-10, comes with a minor version and is listed here.

psychnets 0.4.3

CRAN release: 2026-07-30

  • First CRAN release.
  • The moderated mixed graphical model (mgm_fit(moderators = )) runs on psychnets’ own base-R solver; every estimator is base R by default, with glmnet and glasso as optional engines (native = FALSE).
  • “Network reliability” and “Visualizing networks” are website articles at https://pak.dynasite.org/psychnets.
